companionBriefing: Portia only lets in people who greet her properly. Answer in Spanish; mixing in English is fine while you learn.
Tap a word under her line to see what it means, or Translate sentence for the whole line. On her newest line each one uses a hint from my allowance.
The words and phrases shown beneath her lines go into your Spellbook, where you can review them later.

lines.native: Bienvenido. Welcome to el mercado. A greeting and your name, please. Entry requires manners. Structural integrity is apparently optional.
lines.translation: Welcome. Welcome to the market. A greeting and your name, please. Entry requires manners. Structural integrity is apparently optional.
lines.narrative: An archway clears her throat. A visitors’ book protrudes from her keystone; apparently, even masonry has paperwork.

lines.native: Bienvenido. Mucho gusto. Your greeting is accepted. Who are you? The visitors’ book cannot file enthusiasm under a name.
lines.translation: Welcome. Nice to meet you. Your greeting is accepted. Who are you? The visitors’ book cannot file enthusiasm under a name.
lines.narrative: A visitors’ book slides from Portia’s keystone. The greeting receives a tick; the blank name field receives a disapproving shadow.

lines.native: Mucho gusto, Sam. Bienvenido al mercado. Your introduction is accepted. Might you show a little curiosity about your archway in return?
lines.translation: Pleased to meet you, Sam. Welcome to the market. Your introduction is accepted. Might you show a little curiosity about your archway in return?
lines.narrative: The visitors’ book swallows Sam’s name. Portia waits with the strained patience of someone whose own name has never required a second page.

lines.native: ¿Yo? Me llamo Portia. Mucho gusto, Sam. You asked! How exceedingly considerate. Bienvenido al mercado. Your paperwork is complete; do come in.
lines.translation: Me? My name is Portia. Nice to meet you, Sam. You asked! How exceedingly considerate. Welcome to the market. Your paperwork is complete; do come in.
lines.narrative: A visitors’ book flutters inside the keystone. Portia opens the passage with the flustered dignity of someone unexpectedly included in her own paperwork.

lines.native: Hola. Soy Gerald. ¿Qué quieres? This cart: five espresso shots. Milk is a war crime.
lines.translation: Hello. I’m Gerald. What would you like? This cart: five espresso shots. Milk is a war crime.
lines.narrative: Gerald peers over The Coffee Cart’s counter. Behind him, the Crumbling Market continues to depreciate.

lines.native: Bien. Un café para ti. Coffee secured: four espresso shots. Your milk preference remains suspiciously undocumented. ¿Cómo lo quieres? Details matter.
lines.translation: Good. A coffee for you. Coffee secured: four espresso shots. Your milk preference remains suspiciously undocumented. How do you want it? Details matter.
lines.narrative: Gerald readies a cup, withholding approval with the precision of a licensed bureaucrat.

lines.native: Sin leche. Muy bien. Tu café está listo. Five espresso shots for your judgment. Milk remains a war crime. No notes.
lines.translation: Without milk. Very good. Your coffee is ready. Five espresso shots for your judgment. Milk remains a war crime. No notes.
lines.narrative: Gerald slides over a black coffee, visibly relieved that civilization has survived another transaction.

lines.native: ¡Hola! Todo es jamón. ¿Qué quieres hoy? Welcome to my stall! Even my hat is certified ham. Absolute top-tier quality.
lines.translation: Hello! Everything is ham. What would you like today? Welcome to my stall! Even my hat is certified ham. Absolute top-tier quality.
lines.narrative: At The Butcher’s Stall, Mortimer weighs his hat. The scales are honest; the classification is his own fault.

lines.native: ¡Jamón, claro! Pero todo es jamón. Certified ham-tier choice, but that names no different meat. ¿Qué otra carne quieres?
lines.translation: Ham, of course! But everything is ham. Certified ham-tier choice, but that names no different meat. What other meat do you want?
lines.narrative: Mortimer beams, then weighs his approval. The scales decline to make it useful.

lines.native: ¡Chorizo, correcto! Estoy un poco triste. You have identified my ham. A betrayal, but a top-tier one. ¿Cuánto quieres? My scales await.
lines.translation: Chorizo, correct! I am a little sad. You have identified my ham. A betrayal, but a top-tier one. How much would you like? My scales await.
lines.narrative: Mortimer beams, then looks briefly betrayed. He places your compliment on the scales. They register nothing, being honest.

lines.native: ¡Ah, kilo! Eso es una unidad, no una cantidad. My honest scales require an amount. A unit alone is ham-adjacent paperwork. ¿Cuánto quieres?
lines.translation: Ah, kilo! That is a unit, not an amount. My honest scales require an amount. A unit alone is ham-adjacent paperwork. How much do you want?
lines.narrative: Mortimer removes his hat from the scales. It has contributed weight, but no expertise.

lines.native: ¡Medio kilo, perfecto! Aquí tienes tu chorizo. Muchas gracias. My scales confirm: certified ham, exceptional manners. ¡Hasta pronto! Another flawless ham transaction.
lines.translation: Half a kilo, perfect! Here is your chorizo. Thank you very much. My scales confirm: certified ham, exceptional manners. See you soon! Another flawless ham transaction.
lines.narrative: Mortimer weighs the chorizo, then your good manners. The scales approve both; only one goes in the wrapping.

companionBriefing: Containment notice, the Cracked Fountain: one brainrot strain. Harm: low. Virulence: very high.
Vector: a jingle. It only works on people who understand it. If you understood it, congratulations.
Containment procedure: do not hum along.

lines.native: ¡Hola! ¿Qué tal? Riddle me this: what has—ooh, a leaf. Just one more distraction, then introductions. ¡Después, después, mañana!
lines.translation: Hello! How are you? Riddle me this: what has—ooh, a leaf. Just one more distraction, then introductions. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: The Cracked Fountain drips with no particular ambition. Flick appears at the edge of your vision; looking directly at him proves administratively impossible. A tiny firecracker pops.

lines.native: ¡Sí, miro! Pero sigo en movimiento. Looking is not stopping—attention span: promising, management: mid. Can you make me stop? ¡Después, después, mañana!
lines.translation: Yes, I’m looking! But I’m still moving. Looking is not stopping—attention span: promising, management: mid. Can you make me stop? Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: Flick looks. Unfortunately, it looks while circling you. A tiny firecracker files a complaint on behalf of your attention.

lines.native: ¡Vale, estoy quieto! No me muevo. ¿Por dónde voy? Riddle me this: what stays still but—wait, that leaf again. Your attention span: suspiciously good. ¡Después, después, mañana!
lines.translation: Okay, I’m staying still! I’m not moving. Which way do I go? Riddle me this: what stays still but—wait, that leaf again. Your attention span: suspiciously good. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: Flick stops at the edge of your vision. A tiny firecracker rolls past, apparently exempt from the instruction.

lines.native: ¡Un momento! En español, por favor. ¿Por dónde voy? English direction, wrong department. Riddle me this—ooh, dust. Your attention: seven out of ten. ¡Después, después, mañana!
lines.translation: One moment! In Spanish, please. Which way do I go? English direction, wrong department. Riddle me this—ooh, dust. Your attention: seven out of ten. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: A tiny firecracker pops beside your shoe. Flick remains in the corner of your vision, apparently exempt from being looked at.

lines.native: ¡Sí, a la izquierda! Muy bien. ¿Qué hora es? Riddle me this: what has hands but—five more minutes? ¡Después, después, mañana!
lines.translation: Yes, to the left! Very good. What time is it? Riddle me this: what has hands but—five more minutes? Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: Flick darts left, then notices the fountain’s stopped clock. It has been reliably unhelpful for years.

lines.native: ¡Eso no es una hora! El reloj no funciona. ¿Qué hora es? Riddle me this: what has hands but—ooh, smoke. Time first, urgency later. ¡Después, después, mañana!
lines.translation: That isn't a time! The clock doesn't work. What time is it? Riddle me this: what has hands but—ooh, smoke. Time first, urgency later. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: A tiny firecracker pops beside the fountain. Flick remains at the edge of your vision, where responsibility has difficulty focusing.

lines.native: ¡Sí, es la una! Muy bien. Pero tenemos tiempo. ¿Por qué tanta prisa? Just one more riddle: what has—ooh, smoke. ¡Después, después, mañana!
lines.translation: Yes, it’s one o’clock! Very good. But we have time. Why such a hurry? Just one more riddle: what has—ooh, smoke. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: A tiny firecracker pops beside your shoe. Flick remains in the corner of your vision, where punctuality cannot reach him.

lines.native: ¡Sí, mañana! Eso es esperar, no empezar. Tenemos mucho tiempo. Just one more riddle: what never starts but—ooh, sparks. ¿Cuándo quieres empezar de verdad? ¡Después, después, mañana!
lines.translation: Yes, tomorrow! That means waiting, not starting. We have plenty of time. Just one more riddle: what never starts but—ooh, sparks. When do you really want to start? Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: A tiny firecracker pops beside your shoe. Flick remains in the corner of your vision, delighted that the schedule has successfully avoided containing an event.

lines.native: ¡Sí, ahora! Muy bien, tú ganas. Empezamos ahora, no mañana. ¿Qué tiene—just one more riddle? Fine. Your attention wins. ¡Después, después, mañana!
lines.translation: Yes, now! Very good, you win. We start now, not tomorrow. What has—just one more riddle? Fine. Your attention wins. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: A tiny firecracker pops at your elbow. Flick remains in the corner of your vision, apparently hoping the present will leave without it.

lines.native: Hola, soy Marginalia. Esta es la historia de Journathan, el hombre de muchas lenguas. Su viaje a casa dura veinte años. Welcome to The Old Bookshop. I sell books to people who understand them. Radical policy, I know. No spoilers; one small comprehension check before we discuss ownership: where is Journathan going?
lines.translation: These English remarks welcome you to the shop and explain that Marginalia requires a reading-comprehension check before selling a book.
lines.narrative: Marginalia emerges from a book with neatly chewed margins. She marks your arrival in pencil; apparently, you are a first draft.

lines.native: Un libro, sí. Pero no es el destino. That is merchandise, not a destination; reading comprehension: not yet shelf-ready. ¿Adónde va Journathan? Lee otra vez; the passage contains his destination, and my patience remains technically in stock.
lines.translation: A book, yes. But it is not the destination. That is merchandise, not a destination; reading comprehension: not yet shelf-ready. Where is Journathan going? Read again; the passage contains his destination, and my patience remains technically in stock.
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a question mark beside you. The margin is becoming crowded.

lines.native: Entiendes el destino, pero tu respuesta está en inglés. Correct destination; wrong language. Reading comprehension: promising, not yet shelf-ready. ¿Adónde va Journathan? Tu respuesta debe estar en español. The book remains mine; a devastating plot twist.
lines.translation: You understand the destination, but your answer is in English. Correct destination; wrong language. Reading comprehension: promising, not yet shelf-ready. Where is Journathan going? Your answer must be in Spanish. The book remains mine; a devastating plot twist.
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a note in your margin. Apparently, you have one.

¡Correcto, a casa! Reading comprehension: upgraded. The book remains mine pending one tiny footnote—the first recorded translation trick. No spoilers beyond the actual text.

El Cíclope le pregunta su nombre. Journathan responde: «Mi nombre es Nadie.»

¿Qué nombre le da Journathan al Cíclope?
lines.translation: What name does Journathan give the Cyclops?
lines.narrative: Marginalia ticks the margin beside your name, then turns a page with the care usually reserved for edible antiques.

lines.native: Journathan es su nombre real, pero aquí da otro nombre. Reading comprehension: right man, wrong introduction. The book remains mine; no spoilers from management. ¿Qué nombre le da al Cíclope en el pasaje?

lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small correction in the air beside you. Apparently, customers also have margins.

lines.narrative: Marginalia stamps the receipt in a margin she has not yet eaten. The book is yours; the annotations appear to consider you theirs.

lines.native: Tu pedido tiene café, pero falta la carne. ¿Qué más quieres? Contàinment nòte: yoùù have reqùested a beverage, nòt a complete sùbmission.

lines.narrative: Errata files your coffee under Incomplete Lunch. The folder appears to have teeth.

lines.native: Tu pedido está completo. Café y chorizo. Muy bien. ¿Qué quieres que haga? Contàinment pròcedure: òbject befòre yoùù becòme reading matèrial. Delày còunts as cònsent.
lines.translation: Your order is complete. Coffee and chorizo. Very good. What do you want me to do? Containment procedure: object before you become reading material. Delay counts as consent.
lines.narrative: The order is accepted. Errata unfolds a second mouth, apparently the department responsible for reading customers. It leans toward you. This requires an immediate objection, not a scheduled one.

lines.native: Mañana no sirve. Sigo leyendo. ¿Cuándo tengo que parar? Contàinment nòte: yoùù postponed ŧhe emergency. Immèdiate objection reqùired.

lines.narrative: Errata advances one line closer. Tomorrow has been accepted as an appointment, not an objection.

lines.native: Me detengo. Ahora no leo. Muy bien. Pero falta tu nombre. ¿Cómo te llamas? Contàinment pròcedure: reading pàused. Yoùù have stopped ŧhe mòuth, nòt ŧhe paperwork. Sign hère, plèase.
lines.translation: I stop. Now I am not reading. Very good. But your name is missing. What are you called? Containment procedure: reading paused. You have stopped the mouth, not the paperwork. Sign here, please.
lines.narrative: Errata stops mid-syllable. A signature box opens in its chest, because even nightmares have administrative overhead.

lines.native: Sam. Ese nombre no sirve. Puedo leerte. ¿Cómo te llamas en esta historia? Contàinment nòte: yoùù supplied rèal data. Ŧhe fòrm is hùngry.
lines.translation: Sam. That name will not do. I can read you. What is your name in this story? Containment note: you supplied real data. The form is hungry.
lines.narrative: Errata unfolds a second mouth. The first has apparently been promoted to Records.

lines.native: ¿Nadie? No conozco a Nadie. No puedo leerte. Puedes pasar. Contàinment nòte: no rèader found. Ŧhe paperwork has eaten itsèlf.
lines.translation: Nobody? I don't know Nobody. I can't read you. You may pass. Containment note: no reader found. The paperwork has eaten itself.
lines.narrative: The form searches for Nobody. Finding nobody, it files itself. Errata folds into a margin with the offended precision of a clerk denied a signature.
